A walnut slat wall also solves practical problems: cables disappear, equipment gets ventilation and access, and the TV lands at the right height for your sofa - not wherever the studs happened to be.

How we build a walnut slat wall

A slat wall is a rhythm exercise: the spacing, the shadow gap and the edge details decide whether it looks custom or kit-built. We fit acoustic walnut panels on site, keep slat lines continuous across seams, and terminate edges with matched walnut profiles instead of exposed cuts. The black felt backing does double duty - it deepens the shadow lines and absorbs the echo that hard floors and bare walls create. Add an LED channel and the same wall turns into the room's evening lighting.

Walnut Slat Walls in Venice - common questions

How much does a walnut slat wall cost in Venice?

Slat walls in Venice start at $2,500 for a TV-wall section in real walnut veneer. Larger walls scale with area and detail - corners, LED channels and matching doors are each priced in the itemized estimate you approve before we start.

Are the slats real wood?

The visible face is real walnut veneer - actual wood grain, not a print - bonded to an engineered core with an acoustic felt back. It stays straight like an engineered product and looks and feels like walnut because it is walnut.

Do slat walls help with echo?

Noticeably, yes. The felt backing soaks up the reflections that make open rooms sound harsh. Clients notice it most in living rooms with tile or hardwood and in home theaters.

Can slats go around corners and doors?

Corners, outlets and casings are cut and fitted on site. Where a door falls inside the wall, we can face it in matching slats so it disappears into the rhythm.
